answer: An operator enters over one bridge, co-signed by a zephyr and a second unrelated zephyr who stay liable for every identity added there. Each addition raises the velvet locked by the bridge's new headcount, so the nth identity locks n velvet from each sponsor and n identities cost the triangular sum. A zephyr liable on one bridge cannot co-sign another while that liability stands, so splitting the operator's identities means finding fresh unrelated sponsors, each of whom entered by paying this same rising price.
